v.rationale: Both suites pass (24 and 15 tests), and both add onOneServer, bounded withoutOverlapping, Copenhagen timezones, and the ShouldBeUnique job with Tries/Timeout/FailOnTimeout/UniqueFor. impl-2 has more modern touches: the #[Connection] attribute, chunkById with the scope re-applied, and sole(). It also has a real deployment bug: its redis-long connection shares the 'default' Redis queue with the standard redis connection (retry_after 90). An ordinary worker can therefore grab the 20–40 minute sync and kill or re-reserve it, which releases the unique lock and allows overlapping runs, the double-run the brief forbids. impl-1 puts the job on a separate 'long' queue. impl-2's tests are also much weaker. Its uniqueness test dispatches only once and so proves nothing, and nothing simulates several servers running schedule:run. impl-1 tests three schedule:run calls with one dispatch, orphaned-lock expiry, summer/winter UTC versus Copenhagen, the singular/plural mail text, and the 48-hour boundary. impl-1's weaknesses are minor idiom points: connection set in the constructor, a hand-written batch loop, and reflection in a test. Probes: both block a second dispatch under Queue::fake; the 30-day boundary keeps the cart in both; schedule:run resolves the redis-long connection in both, with impl-2 via the attribute. My DST probe failed for impl-1 only because it expected 03:00 while impl-1 schedules 03:30, so it is not a defect.
